abstract: We investigate features in the primordial power spectrum from inflation, specifically those predicted by the axion monodromy model, using recent observational data. In order to compute posteriors, profile likelihoods and Bayesian evidence accurately for the complex likelihood surfaces arising in this model we have used the CLiENT emulator framework. As our data combinations we use both a "conservative" set consisting of Planck PR4 temperature, polarisation and lensing data together with DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more "aggressive" set which also includes small-scale CMB data from ACT and SPT. We find no robust oscillatory feature in current data. With the conservative data the best fit lies at a frequency $ω\simeq 51$ and lowers $χ^2$ by 10.1 relative to a featureless spectrum. However, this feature is disfavoured by the more aggressive data combination, whose best fit lies at $ω\simeq 31$ and lowers $χ^2$ by 7.4. Fits to featureless data are known to give similar improvements, and the Akaike information criterion, the Bayes factors and the look-elsewhere effect all indicate that neither improvement is significant. The amplitude is limited to $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.056$ and $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.062$ (95%) for the two datasets. The emulators reproduce the true log-likelihood at samples of their posteriors with rms errors of 0.07 and 0.16, and the profile likelihoods are calculated with the true likelihood, using the profile capability of CLiENT.
